hypothesis: If the claim holds, paleotemperature records from both hemispheres will show their coldest glacial interval at the same time within a short lag.
pass_criterion: In at least 80% of paired northern and southern Last Glacial Maximum records, the timing of the coldest interval differs by <= 3 kyr, and the cross-correlation of northern and southern composites peaks within +/-3 kyr of zero lag.
fail_criterion: Median lag between north and south temperature minima is > 5 kyr, or the cross-correlation peak falls outside +/-5 kyr.
interpretation: 'Simultaneous' is read as coincident within dating uncertainty, about a few thousand years. 'Temperature of the whole world cooler' is measured by ice-core isotope and marine proxy temperatures from both hemispheres.

dataset.name: NOAA NCEI Paleoclimatology Data (ice core and marine temperature records)
dataset.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
dataset.why_it_fits: Hosts Greenland and Antarctic ice-core isotope series and marine sediment proxies with age models, giving timing of coldest glacial intervals in both hemispheres.
